rules.title: Eviction for Failure to Pay Rent Increase
rules.requirement: A landlord may file a suit for eviction if a tenant fails to pay rent after being given notice of a rent increase and a Notice to Quit, provided the rent increase is not unconscionable and complies with all laws or municipal ordinances. A Notice to Quit must be served at least one month prior to filing the suit.
rules.summary_plain: If your landlord raises your rent and you don't pay, they can evict you only if they gave you at least one month notice and the increase is fair and legal.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si su casero aumenta su renta y usted no paga, pueden desalojarlo solo si le dieron un aviso de al menos un mes y el aumento es justo y legal.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to tenants who fail to pay rent after a rent increase notice.
rules.quoted_span: If a tenant fails to pay rent after being given notice of a rent increase and a Notice to Quit, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. The rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(f)).

rules.title: Eviction for Health and Safety Violations or Removal from Rental Market
rules.requirement: A tenant may be evicted if the landlord must board up, demolish, or remove the property from the rental market due to substantial health and safety violations or illegal occupancy, with a Notice to Quit served at least three months before filing suit. Relocation assistance must be provided before eviction.
rules.summary_plain: You can be evicted if your landlord must close or demolish the property for health or safety reasons, but they must give you 3 months notice and help you relocate first.
rules.summary_plain_es: Puede ser desalojado si su casero debe cerrar o demoler la propiedad por razones de salud o seguridad, pero deben darle un aviso de 3 meses y ayudarle a reubicarse primero.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies when landlord must board up, demolish, or remove property due to health/safety violations or illegal occupancy.
rules.quoted_span: A tenant may be evicted if the following conditions apply: 1) The landlord has been cited by an inspector and needs to board up or demolish the property because of substantial health and safety violations and because it is financially difficult to abate the violations. ... A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three months before filing a suit for eviction. The tenant can’t be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.

rules.title: Eviction for Permanent Retirement of Property from Residential Use
rules.requirement: If a landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential use (not covered by health and safety removal), they must serve a Notice to Quit at least 18 months before filing suit for eviction and cannot take legal action until the lease expires.
rules.summary_plain: If your landlord wants to stop renting the building permanently, they must give you 18 months notice before suing to evict you and wait until your lease ends.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si su casero quiere dejar de alquilar el edificio permanentemente, debe darle un aviso de 18 meses antes de demandar para desalojarlo y esperar hasta que termine su contrato.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies when landlord wants to permanently retire property from residential use, excluding health and safety removal cases.
rules.quoted_span: If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord may file suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months prior to filing the suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(h)).

rules.title: Eviction for Refusal to Accept Reasonable Lease Changes
rules.requirement: When a lease expires, if a tenant refuses reasonable but substantial changes proposed by the landlord after written notice, the landlord may file suit for eviction with at least one month Notice to Quit.
rules.summary_plain: If your lease ends and you refuse reasonable changes your landlord proposes, they can evict you after giving you one month notice.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si su contrato termina y usted rechaza cambios razonables que propone su casero, pueden desalojarlo después de darle un aviso de un mes.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies at lease expiration when tenant refuses reasonable changes to lease terms after written notice.
rules.exemptions_text: Protections apply to senior citizens and disabled tenants under specific acts.
rules.quoted_span: When the lease expires, the landlord may propose reasonable but substantial changes to the terms and conditions of the lease. If after written notice the tenant refuses to accept those changes the landlord may file a suit for eviction... A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month before filing suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(i)).

rules.title: Eviction for Continuous Failure to Pay Rent or Habitual Late Payment
rules.requirement: If a tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late after a written Notice to Cease, the landlord may file suit for eviction with at least one month Notice to Quit.
rules.summary_plain: If you keep paying rent late or not at all after being warned, your landlord can evict you with one month notice.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si sigue pagando la renta tarde o no la paga después de una advertencia, su casero puede desalojarlo con un aviso de un mes.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies when tenant habitually pays rent late or fails to pay after written Notice to Cease.
rules.quoted_span: If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, after written Notice to Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month before filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(j)).

rules.title: Eviction for Conversion to Condominium, Cooperative, or Fee Simple Ownership
rules.requirement: If a landlord converts a building or mobile home park to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership, they may file suit for eviction with a Notice to Quit served at least three years before filing. No action may be taken until the lease expires. Courts may grant stays of eviction under certain conditions.
rules.summary_plain: If your landlord converts the property to condos or co-ops, they must give you 3 years notice before suing to evict you and wait until your lease ends.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si su casero convierte la propiedad en condominios o cooperativas, debe darle un aviso de 3 años antes de demandar para desalojarlo y esperar hasta que termine su contrato.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to conversions of rental property to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership.
rules.exemptions_text: Senior citizens and disabled tenants with protected tenancy status are exempt from eviction during protected periods.
rules.quoted_span: If the landlord or owner of a building or mobile home park is converting the property from the rental market to a condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership... A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three years before filing a suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(k)).

rules.title: Eviction for Tenancy After Conversion to Condominium, Cooperative, or Fee Simple Ownership
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict tenants whose tenancy began after recording of the master deed or cooperative agreement if the owner or buyer seeks to personally occupy the unit, with a Notice to Quit served at least two months prior to filing suit. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires.
rules.summary_plain: If you started renting after the property was converted to condos or co-ops, the owner can evict you if they or a buyer wants to live there, but they must give you 2 months notice and wait until your lease ends.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si comenzó a alquilar después de que la propiedad se convirtió en condominios o cooperativas, el propietario puede desalojarlo si él o un comprador quiere vivir allí, pero debe darle un aviso de 2 meses y esperar hasta que termine su contrato.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to tenants whose initial tenancy began after recording of master deed or cooperative agreement.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may file for eviction, if the owner of a building or mobile home park, which is constructed as or being converted to a condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership, seeks to evict a tenant or sublessee whose initial tenancy began after the master deed, or agreement establishing the cooperative or subdivision plat was recorded... A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least two months prior to filing suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(l)).

rules.title: Eviction for Termination of Employment-Based Tenancy
rules.requirement: If a tenant resides on the condition of employment by the landlord and that employment is terminated, the landlord may file suit for eviction with a Notice to Quit served three days prior to filing.
rules.summary_plain: If you live in your rental because you work for the landlord and your job ends, they can evict you with 3 days notice.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si vive en su alquiler porque trabaja para el casero y su trabajo termina, pueden desalojarlo con un aviso de 3 días.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to tenants residing on condition of employment by landlord as superintendent, janitor, or similar.
rules.quoted_span: If a tenant resides in the property on the condition that, he is employed by the landlord as a superintendent, janitor, or in some other job and that employment is terminated the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant three days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(m)).

rules.title: Eviction for Conviction of Drug Offense Committed on the Property
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant convicted of drug offenses committed on the property if the tenant has not completed or is not participating in a drug rehabilitation program. A Notice to Quit must be served at least three days prior to filing suit. Eviction suits must be brought within two years of conviction or release.
rules.summary_plain: If you are convicted of drug crimes on the property and don't complete rehab, your landlord can evict you with 3 days notice, but only within two years of conviction or release.
rules.summary_plain_es: Si es condenado por delitos de drogas en la propiedad y no completa rehabilitación, su casero puede desalojarlo con un aviso de 3 días, pero solo dentro de dos años de la condena o liberación.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to tenants convicted of drug offenses on the property who have not completed or are not in rehab.
rules.exemptions_text: Does not apply to tenants allowing juveniles found delinquent for drug use or possession to reside.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may file a suit for eviction, if the tenant... has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to drug offenses that took place on the property, and has not in connection with his sentence either (1) successfully completed or (2) been admitted to and continues during probation participation toward completion of a drug rehabilitation program... A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(n)).
